subsystem.name: VehiclePhysics
subsystem.responsibility: Collision subsystem lifecycle and result plumbing: a large family of trivial registration/teardown stubs that forward nullsub placeholder function pointers through BooleanToIntConversion, plus real collision logic addressing a byte-property region at object offset 636, a proxy active-id word list at +0xC88, per-index clamped float parameters, conditional property dispatch and typed collision result processing. Concrete owning classes are not proven; class groupings are GUESS semantic clusters over UnknownObject packet owners.

summary: DERIVED proposal for the vehicle_physics scope. The packet contains 50 functions: 44 trivial lifecycle stubs (30 registration-styled, 14 teardown-styled) that each read a nullsub placeholder function pointer and return BooleanToIntConversion (0x00587B3E) applied to that address - the legacy names suggest collision registration/teardown hook points, but every body is behaviorally identical and wraps a no-op, so the real handlers and the consumers of the returned status are unknown. Six real functions carry the actual collision logic: CollisionNodePropertySetter writes a byte at (a2+636), CollisionDataFill memset32s 256 bytes at offset 636, CollisionProxyUnregister maintains the active proxy-id word list at +0xC88 and per-proxy state, CollisionParameterClampAndStore clamps three floats and stores them at per-index offsets, ConditionalCollisionDispatch gates CollisionNodePropertySetter on a guard field at +0x0, and CollisionResultProcessing resolves a typed collision result into activation (+0x24) and magnitude (+0x28) outputs. All 50 required functions are covered exactly once; every callee, field and global is reported verbatim from the packet. Owners remain UnknownObject in the packet; the class/interface organization is a conservative GUESS layer on top, with uncertain structure left in unresolved rather than forced.

Byte-property setter (thiscall): writes the caller-supplied byte a3 into the object at byte offset (a2 + 636) and returns a3; invoked by SwapAndReinit (0x00452740), ConditionalCollisionDispatch (0x004527C0) and CameraViewportConfigBatch (0x00453560).

Block fill (fastcall): builds a three-byte-lane fill pattern from byte a3 (value|value<<8|value<<16) and memset32s 0x40 dwords (256 bytes) at offset 636 of the object; invoked by HWInput_Post (0x00455E70).

Proxy-slot unregister: clears the active-flag byte at this+0x37C, scans the active proxy-id word list at this+0xC88 (up to 256 entries) and clears the matched entry, and resets the per-proxy dword at this+0x87C+4*a2 to 0.0 or dbl_8AFEA8+a3 depending on the sign of a3.

Collision parameter clamp-and-store: clamps a4/a5 into [0.0, 1.0] and a3 at a 0.0 lower bound, then stores them at float index a2+8 (byte 0x20+4*a2), a2+190 (byte 0x2F8+4*a2) and a2 (byte 4*a2); returns the D3DTextureStage (0x0044F8F0) result on both branches.

Conditional collision-node property dispatch: when the guard dword at this+0x0 is zero, calls CollisionNodePropertySetter (0x0044F050) with byte_7CA594, this[1] and this[2] and returns its result; the non-zero guard path returns without dispatching.

Collision result processing selected by the type field at this+0x0: early zero-output when ConditionalFlagReturn(&dword_5EA43C) is set and dword_7C569C equals 5; type 0 reads a packed flag via PackedFlagRead(byte_7CA594, this[1]); type 1 reads activation from *(this+0x1C)+0x10; type 2 takes the absolute value of the float at *(this+0x20)+4 as the magnitude and derives a 0/1 activation state from a 0.5 threshold. Writes activation at +0x24 and magnitude at +0x28.

classes.name: CollisionRegistrationHooks
classes.responsibility: Semantic grouping (GUESS) of the 30 legacy collision-registration stubs (CollisionCallbackRegistration*, CollisionModuleRegister*, CollisionStaticDataRegistration*, CollisionDataRegistrationBlock*, CollisionInitRegistration/Wrapper/Delegator, ThunkCollisionInit*, CollisionConstructorThunk*, CollisionCallbackRegister*). Every member reads a nullsub placeholder function pointer and returns BooleanToIntConversion (0x00587B3E) applied to that address; no registration side effect is visible. Packet owners are UnknownObject; class boundaries are not proven.

classes.name: CollisionNodePropertyRegion
classes.responsibility: Functions addressing a byte-indexed property region whose base lies at offset 636 (0x27C) of a caller-supplied object: CollisionNodePropertySetter writes one byte at (index + 636) and CollisionDataFill fills 256 bytes at 636 with a uniform pattern. The two functions never occur in the same frame path in this packet, so common ownership of the 636-offset region is GUESS.

classes.name: CollisionProxy
classes.responsibility: Collision proxy-slot bookkeeping (single evidenced method): CollisionProxyUnregister clears the active-flag byte, removes the proxy id from the active word list at +0xC88 and resets the per-proxy dword. The +0x37C and +0x87C offsets are DERIVED from behavior and not struct-confirmed.

classes.name: CollisionParameterStore
classes.responsibility: Stores clamped per-index float collision parameters at float indices a2, a2+8 and a2+190 (byte offsets 4*a2, 0x20+4*a2, 0x2F8+4*a2). The D3DTextureStage call in the body is treated as a likely decompiler artifact; the clamp-and-store role is the evidenced core.

classes.name: CollisionDispatch
classes.responsibility: Conditional dispatch that forwards a byte collision-node property to CollisionNodePropertySetter when the guard field at this+0x0 is zero.

classes.name: CollisionResultProcessor
classes.responsibility: Collision result resolution: selects a result type at this+0x0 (0=packed flag, 1=object field, 2=axis), computes an activation value and magnitude, and stores them at this+0x24 and this+0x28. Field names are DERIVED from usage; the type-enum values are unproven.

interfaces.name: CollisionLifecycleHook
interfaces.purpose: The 44 trivial registration/teardown stubs share one observable shape: each reads a function pointer (a nullsub placeholder) and returns BooleanToIntConversion (0x00587B3E) applied to that address, producing a constant non-zero status integer. A replacement exposing the same lifecycle hook points would preserve the int(void) signature and the forwarding behavior; the status meaning is not evidenced.

compatibility_contracts.name: CollisionNodePropertyRegion
compatibility_contracts.description: CollisionNodePropertySetter (0x0044F050) writes one byte at byte offset (a2+636) of a caller object and CollisionDataFill (0x0044F070) fills 256 bytes (0x40 dwords) at offset 636 with a three-lane pattern derived from one byte. Callers SwapAndReinit (0x00452740), ConditionalCollisionDispatch (0x004527C0), CameraViewportConfigBatch (0x00453560) and HWInput_Post (0x00455E70) depend on this region; a replacement must preserve the region offset and byte semantics.

compatibility_contracts.name: CollisionResultOutputs
compatibility_contracts.description: CollisionResultProcessing (0x00453100) writes an activation value at result+0x24 and a magnitude at result+0x28, selected by the type field at result+0x0, and reads the packed-flag parameter at +0x4, an object reference at +0x1C and an axis reference at +0x20. A replacement must reproduce the same result outputs and type dispatch.

compatibility_contracts.name: CollisionProxyActiveIdList
compatibility_contracts.description: CollisionProxyUnregister (0x0044F0E0) maintains an active proxy-id word list at object+0xC88 (up to 256 entries), a per-proxy active-flag byte at +0x37C and a per-proxy dword at +0x87C+4*a2; unregistering clears the matching list entry and resets the dword to 0.0 or dbl_8AFEA8+a3. A replacement must preserve the list and flag semantics. Offsets +0x37C/+0x87C are DERIVED from usage.

compatibility_contracts.name: CollisionLifecycleHookStatus
compatibility_contracts.description: The 44 registration/teardown stubs return the integer produced by BooleanToIntConversion (0x00587B3E) applied to a nullsub function pointer. Because the wrapped routines are no-ops, the returned status is a constant non-zero value; a replacement that materializes these lifecycle hooks must keep the int(void) signature, but the status semantics are not evidenced.

unresolved: All 44 registration/teardown stubs wrap nullsub (no-op) placeholder routines through BooleanToIntConversion (0x00587B3E); the real handlers they stand for, and the consumers of the returned status, are unknown and no callers are recorded.
The exact semantics of BooleanToIntConversion (registration vs status conversion) are not established by this packet; every stub only forwards whatever integer the helper produces.

Common ownership of the 636-offset (0x27C) byte region by CollisionNodePropertySetter and CollisionDataFill is GUESS: the two functions operate on caller-supplied objects and do not co-occur in a shared frame path in this packet.

The D3DTextureStage (0x0044F8F0) call inside CollisionParameterClampAndStore is treated as a likely decompiler artifact; the clamp-and-store role is the evidenced core, but the call's true role is unresolved.
The type-enum values (0=packed flag, 1=object field, 2=axis) in CollisionResultProcessing and the magic session value 5 in dword_7C569C are not established by this packet.
CollisionProxyUnregister offsets +0x37C (active flag) and +0x87C+4*a2 (per-proxy dword) are DERIVED from behavior and are not present as allowed field refs; their struct identity is unconfirmed.
global:0x0059E880 is listed for CollisionResultProcessing but does not appear in the raw decompiled source; it may back the 0.5 threshold or related physics data, but its role is unresolved.
byte_7CA594 is read by ConditionalCollisionDispatch and CollisionResultProcessing but its type and role are resolved elsewhere; it is consumed here as an opaque argument.

Legacy ABI names (registration/teardown/init/sound-unregister/grid-free/resource-release variants) are UNKNOWN-trust labels from the corpus and are not verified against body evidence; the 44 stubs are behaviorally identical.
No genuine state machine is evidenced: CollisionResultProcessing's type dispatch is a selector, not a stateful transition graph, so state_machines is left empty.
